summary: Michael Comans is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong. He held posts at the University of Sydney and Sri Venkateswara Temple.
Michael J. Conway specializes in Buddhist studies. He serves as Lecturer of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and is attested as a faculty member at the Otani Academic Society in 2026.

Michael Coulson (1936–1975) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his B.A. and D.Phil. at the University of Oxford and served as Lecturer and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Edinburgh from 1966 to 1975.

Michael Eido Luetchford works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied electronic engineering at the University of Bradford, trained under Gudo Wafu Nishijima from ~1977 to 2007, and founded Windbell Publications.

Michael Fertig (1801–1873) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Würzburg under Othmar Frank. He taught Latin at the University of Passau (1846) and served as Rector at Hans-Carossa-Gymnasium Landshut (1855–1869).

Michael Friedrich is a Sinologist who earned his PhD from the University of Munich, where he was a Wissenschaftlicher Assistent (1983–1986). He later served as Professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.
Michael G. Morony works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and UCLA, where he became a professor in 1974.

Michael Haberlandt (1860–1940) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Friedrich Müller and Georg Bühler, later teaching there as a privatdozent and professor, and directing Vienna's Natural History Museum in 1911.

Michael Hahn (1941–2014) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau and held academic appointments at the University of Bonn and the University of Marburg.
Michael Harack specializes in religious studies and sinology. He studied at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, earning a Master of Arts (attested 2007).
Michael Hookham is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Chögyam Trungpa in 1965 and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his BA and doctorate at the University of London and held various posts at SOAS, including Head of the South Asia Department and Associate Dean.

Michael I. Como works in religious studies, Japanology, and Sinology, having studied under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. He is a faculty member at Columbia University, attested as Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies in 2026.

Michael J. Sweet (d. 2021) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa among others, and later served as clinical assistant professor in psychiatry.
Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned his Master of Arts at San Diego State University under the supervision of Sandra A. Wawrytko, attested in 2011.

Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town and the University of California, Santa Barbara, completing his doctoral studies under William F. Powell.

Michael Janda is a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Vienna under Jochem Schindler and Heiner Eichner, habilitated at the University of Zurich, and was appointed to the Indo-European linguistics chair at the University of Münster in 2002.

Michael Jansen (1947–2022) was an archaeology and Indology scholar. Educated at Bonn, Rome, Delhi, ASI, and RWTH Aachen, he served as Dean of Architecture at RWTH Aachen (1988–1999) and founding rector of the German University of Technology in Oman.

Michael Jerryson (1974–2021) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and UC Santa Barbara under Mark Juergensmeyer, and held professorships at Eckerd College (~2010–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2012–2018).
Michael Kowalewski is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.
